claims.statement: The `step ssh` group ("create and manage ssh certificates") is registered from init() in command/ssh/ssh.go and registers 14 subcommands: certificate, check-host, config, fingerprint, hosts, inspect, list, login, logout, needs-renewal, proxycommand, rekey, renew, and revoke.

command/ssh/ssh.go defines the shared SSH flags: --principal/-n, --host, --host-id, --sign, --password-file, --provisioner-password-file, --add-user, and --private-key; the principal flag documentation notes it cannot be combined with --token for OIDC, JWK, and X5C provisioners, or provisioners with disableCustomSANs, because those provisioners derive principals from the token.
createPrincipalsFromSubject builds default user certificate principals from the sanitized subject, plus the local part of an email subject when different, plus the original subject when different.

The ssh package wraps failures in user-facing helpers: sshConfigErr suggests running `step ssh config`, contactAdminErr suggests contacting an administrator, and debugErr reports an internal step process error.

loginOnUnauthorized builds a CA retry function for HTTP 401: when the CA requires client authentication it generates an OIDC identity token (email required), a default SSH key pair, and an identity CSR, calls SSHSign for a user certificate, writes the X.509 identity, and adds the SSH certificate to the agent.
step ssh certificate takes <key-id> and <key-file> positional arguments and derives the SSH conventions <key-file>.pub and <key-file>-cert.pub for the outputs.

step ssh certificate supports --host, --host-id, --sign, --principal, --password-file, --provisioner-password-file, --add-user, --not-before/--not-after, --token, --comment, --kty/--curve/--size, --no-agent, --min-password-length, and the CA connection flags; --host selects provisioner.SSHHostCert with cautils.SSHHostSignType, otherwise a user certificate with cautils.SSHUserSignType.

step ssh certificate validation rejects --no-password without --insecure, --no-password with --password-file or --min-password-length, --token with --provisioner-password-file, --host with --add-user, --host-id without --host, and --add-user with more than one principal.

With --sign, step ssh certificate parses the existing public key file (and the matching --private-key) instead of generating a key pair, passing the public key to the certificate flow via cautils.WithSSHPublicKey.

When the CA requires client authentication, host certificates get an X.509 identity CSR with a UUID URI SAN: an explicit --host-id UUID, a UUID derived from /etc/machine-id when --host-id is "machine", or the UUID read from an existing default identity certificate to avoid clobbering the host ID on re-runs.
step ssh certificate --add-user generates an extra key pair and requests an add-user provisioner certificate, written to <base>-provisioner, <base>-provisioner.pub, and <base>-provisioner-cert.pub.

step ssh certificate writes the generated private key OpenSSH-format with mode 0600, encrypted with a prompted password (honoring --password-file and --min-password-length) unless --no-password with --insecure; public keys and certificates are written 0644 as authorized-key lines commented with the subject.
Unless --no-agent is passed, step ssh certificate adds a generated user certificate and its private key to the SSH agent with the subject as comment.
deriveMachineID maps /etc/machine-id to a version-4 UUID via a keyed Blake2b-128 hash with the key "man moon machine".
readExistingUUID recovers the host UUID by loading the default identity certificate and parsing its first URI SAN as a UUID.

step ssh login requests an SSH user certificate and adds it to the agent; it requires a running SSH agent, and unless --force is passed it returns early when the agent already holds a key with the subject comment signed by one of the CA's user certificate keys.

step ssh login generates a key pair and an SSH user sign token, calls SSHSign with the principals and optional add-user public key, writes the X.509 identity when the CA requires client authentication, and adds the certificate (and add-user certificate) to the agent via Agent.AddCertificate.

step ssh logout removes keys from the agent: --all with no subject removes every key; otherwise it removes keys matching the subject comment, restricted to keys signed by the CA's user certificate keys when SSH roots are available, or to certificate keys otherwise.

step ssh config renders SSH configuration from CA templates; it supports --host for server config, --roots to print user or host CA public keys, --federation to print all federation keys, --team to bootstrap a team authority, and --set/--set-file template variables, with the roots/federation/set/team flags mutually incompatible in defined combinations.

step ssh config --roots/--federation prints keys in authorized-key format and reports "step certificates is not configured with SSH support" when the CA has no SSH keys configured for the requested type.

step ssh config sends the template data (GOOS, StepPath, StepBasePath, SSH template version v2, the current context name, Console, and --set variables) to client.SSHConfig; for user config it derives the User variable from --set or the first principal of a CA-signed certificate in the agent, failing with a message to run `step ssh login <identity>` when missing, then writes the returned templates or prints them with --dry-run.
step ssh hosts calls client.SSHGetHosts and prints a tab-separated HOSTNAME/ID/TAGS table of valid hosts.

step ssh check-host calls client.SSHCheckHost for a hostname, prints true/false with --verbose, and exits 1 when no certificate exists; when the CA requires client authentication it builds an X.5C one-time token for the /ssh/check-host audience from the default identity.

SSH one-time tokens are typed by the constants in utils/cautils/token_flow.go: SSHUserSignType and SSHHostSignType target /1.0/ssh/sign, SSHRenewType /1.0/ssh/renew, SSHRekeyType /1.0/ssh/rekey, and SSHRevokeType /1.0/ssh/revoke.

step ssh renew renews an SSH host certificate (per its description it cannot renew user certificates): it reads the certificate serial, sets sshpop-cert/sshpop-key on the context for the SSHPOP token, calls SSHRenew, and writes the new certificate (defaulting to overwriting the input) plus any renewed identity certificate.

step ssh rekey generates a new default key pair, calls SSHRekey with the new public key using an SSHPOP token keyed by the existing certificate serial, and writes the new private key (OpenSSH 0600, password-prompted or --password-file), public key, and certificate.
step ssh revoke takes a serial number or derives it from --sshpop-cert, maps --reasonCode to an OCSP revocation code via cmdca.ReasonCodeToNum, and calls SSHRevoke with Passive set to true.

step ssh needs-renewal reports whether a certificate should be renewed based on remaining lifetime: --expires-in accepts a percent threshold (default 66, defaultPercentUsedThreshold) of lifetime used or a duration window, and the exit codes are 0 needs renewal, 1 does not, 2 file missing, 255 other errors.

The bundled systemd/ssh-cert-renewer.timer runs every 15 minutes with a 5-minute randomized delay and drives ssh-cert-renewer.service, whose ExecCondition invokes `step ssh needs-renewal ${CERT_LOCATION}`.

step ssh proxycommand takes <user> <host> <port> for use in an SSH ProxyCommand directive: it ensures the user is logged in, asks the CA for a configured bastion via SSHBastion, and proxies through the bastion or directly.

doLoginIfNeeded checks the agent for a valid CA-signed user key and, if absent, performs the full login flow: generate an SSH user sign token, SSHSign a user certificate, write the X.509 identity when required, and add the certificate to the agent.

The direct proxy opens a TCP connection and copies stdin/stdout in both directions, returning as soon as either direction completes to avoid a deadlock when the server closes first (smallstep/cli#1641).

When a bastion is configured, step ssh proxycommand execs the local ssh binary (falling back to /usr/bin/ssh) with the bastion user, port, and flags, appending either the bastion command rendered by sshutil.ProxyCommand or an nc host port connector.

step ssh inspect reads a certificate from a file or STDIN, falling back from ssh.ParseAuthorizedKey to raw base64 ssh.ParsePublicKey, and prints a text layout or JSON built by sshutil.InspectCertificate.
step ssh list lists the SSH agent's keys filtered by an optional subject comment, printing fingerprints by default or raw authorized keys with --raw.
step ssh fingerprint prints the fingerprint of an SSH public key or certificate using the go.step.sm/crypto/sshutil formatters, with a --format flag (default base64-raw) and a --certificate mode.

internal/sshutil.Agent wraps ssh/agent.ExtendedAgent with its connection; DialAgent connects via SSH_AUTH_SOCK, using Unix sockets on Unix platforms and Unix sockets, Windows pipes at SSH_AUTH_SOCK, or the default OpenSSH pipe on Windows.
On Windows the default SSH agent pipe is \\.\pipe\openssh-ssh-agent, overridable by an IdentityAgent line in the user's ~/.ssh/config.

Agent operations accept variadic AgentOption filters: WithSignatureKey keeps only certificates signed by the given keys, WithCertsOnly keeps only keys that parse as certificates, and WithRemoveExpiredCerts transparently removes certificates whose ValidBefore has passed.

The Agent helper methods are HasKeys, ListKeys, ListCertificates, GetKey, GetSigner, RemoveKeys, and RemoveAllKeys, all built on the option filters; AuthMethod exposes the agent as an ssh.AuthMethod via a public-keys callback.

Agent.AddCertificate adds a certificate with the subject as comment, computing the lifetime from ValidBefore: infinite certificates use lifetime 0, already-expired certificates are rejected, and Windows always uses lifetime 0 because the Windows agent fails with a lifetime.
sshutil.NewCertSigner builds an ssh.Signer that signs with the given certificate and private key, and sshutil.ParseCertificate parses marshaled bytes into an *ssh.Certificate.
sshutil.PublicKey converts an ssh.PublicKey to a crypto.PublicKey, dispatching by key type to RSA, ECDSA (including SK-ECDSA), Ed25519 (including SK-Ed25519), and the insecure DSA legacy type.
sshutil's wire parsers parseRSA, parseECDSA, parseED25519, and parseDSA follow RFC 4253 and RFC 5656 formats, with parseECDSA using crypto/ecdh to build the key from the point bytes.
publicKeyTypeAndSize maps key types to display names and bit sizes, appending -CERT for certificates, and drives certificate inspection.

InspectCertificate converts an *ssh.Certificate into a CertificateInspect with type (host/user/unknown), key and signing-key algorithm plus SHA-256 fingerprints, serial, validity, principals, critical options, extensions, and the raw signature; Validity renders ssh-keygen-style local-time ranges or "forever".

sshutil.Shell dials an SSH server (defaulting the port to 22) using ~/.ssh/known_hosts as the host key callback, with auth defaulting to the SSH agent and replaceable via WithAuthMethod, WithSigner, or WithCertificate; it supports Run, RemoteShell with PTY setup, and LocalForward/RemoteForward port forwarding.
sshutil.ProxyCommand substitutes %%, %h, %p, and %r placeholders in a bastion proxy command.

Adding a new step ssh subcommand means creating command/ssh/<name>.go with a <name>Command() cli.Command and command.ActionFunc action, reusing the shared flags in command/ssh/ssh.go and the CA flags, registering it in the Subcommands list, and building one-time tokens with flow.GenerateSSHToken using the utils/cautils token types.

Extending internal/sshutil means adding key-type handling in PublicKey and publicKeyTypeAndSize with dedicated wire parsers and tests in sshutil_test.go, adding new agent behaviors as AgentOption functions composing with the existing HasKeys/ListKeys/GetKey/RemoveKeys paths, and keeping platform-specific agent dialing in the build-tagged agent_unix.go/agent_windows.go files behind the public DialAgent entry point.
